title: Dispraise
summary: DISPRAISE, noun Dispraze. [dis and praise.] 1. Blame; censure. Be cautious not to speak in dispraise of a competitor. 2. Reproach; dishonor. The general has seen Moors with as bad faces; no dispraise

inlines.v: DISPRAISE, noun Dispraze. [dis and praise.] 1. Blame; censure. Be cautious not to speak in dispraise of a competitor. 2. Reproach; dishonor. The general has seen Moors with as bad faces; no dispraise to Bertrans. DISPRAISE, verb transitive To blame; to censure; to mention with disapprobation, or some degree of reproach. I dispraised him before the wicked.
